items.headline: Anthropic quietly pitches its own AI safety bill to lawmakers
items.summary: Anthropic privately circulated a draft federal bill that would let the Commerce Department ask a court to block release of an AI model only if it poses an imminent risk of over $1 billion in damage or 50+ deaths/serious injuries from bioweapons, loss of control, or cyberattacks. The move is notable because a leading AI lab is shaping the terms of its own regulation, drawing criticism that the threshold is narrow and company-friendly.

items.headline: xAI launches Grok Voice 3.0, a speech-to-speech model for voice agents
items.summary: xAI released Grok Voice 3.0, which processes audio directly rather than chaining speech-to-text, an LLM, and text-to-speech, aimed at phone support, contact centers, and in-app assistants. It replaces Grok Voice 2.0 and is available via xAI's Voice Agent API.

items.headline: Mistral AI puts Large 4 into public preview
items.summary: Mistral AI's newest flagship model, Mistral Large 4, entered public preview, with open weights expected by the end of October. It's a notable step for the French lab as it competes with much larger US and Chinese frontier labs.

items.headline: OpenAI expands GPT-6 access to all ChatGPT users, including free tier
items.summary: After initially limiting GPT-6 Astra to its Daybreak enterprise program, OpenAI began rolling the model out to the entire ChatGPT user base, including free users, significantly widening access to its most capable model to date.

items.headline: Microsoft overhauls Microsoft 365 Copilot's navigation around agents and automation
items.summary: Microsoft restructured Copilot's interface: a standalone 'Agents' entry in Chat is being replaced by 'Plugins,' and 'Automations' is moving into the Home pane for Cowork users, part of a broader push to make Copilot an agentic layer across Microsoft 365.

items.headline: FDA comment period closes on generative AI medical device framework
items.summary: The FDA's Digital Health Center of Excellence is wrapping up public comments (due October 19) on its discussion paper covering generative AI-enabled medical devices, an early step toward formal guidance for diagnostic and clinical AI tools entering an already crowded regulatory list of 1,600+ AI-enabled devices.
items.source: FDA Digital Health Center of Excellence

items.headline: NVIDIA releases Isaac ROS 5.0, bringing agentic AI to the ROS robotics ecosystem
items.summary: NVIDIA shipped Isaac ROS 5.0 at ROSCon in Toronto, adding reusable 'Isaac skills' for manipulation and setup that robots and AI agents can run, plus agent-ready documentation, support for ROS Lyrical/Ubuntu 24.04, and faster GPU-accelerated perception for the roughly 1.3 million-strong ROS developer community.

items.headline: Google DeepMind AI safety researcher publicly resigns over Pentagon AI contract
items.summary: Another Google DeepMind researcher departed citing concerns that the company's AI systems and military contracts are moving faster than internal safety oversight can keep up with, continuing a string of high-profile safety-team exits from the lab in recent months.

items.headline: EU AI Office gains enforcement power over general-purpose AI providers
items.summary: The EU AI Act's GPAI enforcement regime took full effect, giving the AI Office authority to demand documentation, commission independent model evaluations, order corrective action up to market withdrawal, and fine providers up to 3% of global turnover or €15 million for noncompliance.

items.headline: Schaeffler and ROKAE partner to mass-produce humanoid robot joint modules
items.summary: German industrial supplier Schaeffler signed a strategic agreement with Chinese robotics firm ROKAE to co-develop integrated joint modules for humanoid robots, with Schaeffler supplying precision components from its new Taicang 'embodied intelligent robotics' facility as industrial giants race into humanoid manufacturing.
